criteria.description: Patients undergoing minimally invasive cardiac procedures, including percutaneous coronary intervention, transcatheter aortic valve replacement, and catheter ablation.
Population does not undergo minimally invasive cardiac procedures.
Does not evaluate a non-fasting protocol.
Does not include a fasting protocol comparator.
Randomized controlled trials reporting at least one eligible outcome.
Not a randomized controlled trial, such as a review, meta-analysis, or observational study.

At least one of: composite patient satisfaction; hunger; thirst; anxiety; tiredness or fatigue; aspiration; postprocedural pneumonia; emergency endotracheal intubation; nausea or vomiting; anti-emetic use; hypoglycemia (blood glucose at or below 0.7 g/L); intraoperative fluid provision; contrast-induced acute kidney injury; inotropes or vasopressors; need for ventilation.
Confirmed to report none of the eligible outcomes. Missing outcome information in a title or abstract alone is insufficient for exclusion; retain for full-text assessment.

research_question: In patients undergoing minimally invasive cardiac procedures, how do non-fasting protocols compare with fasting protocols for patient satisfaction, procedural safety, and other eligible clinical outcomes?
title: Non-fasting versus fasting before minimally invasive cardiac procedures
